newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish minister against motorway through Warsaw.
newsitem.headline: Polish minister against motorway through Warsaw.

text.p: Poland's environment ministry on Monday said it opposed proposals for a planned Paris-Berlin-Warsaw-Moscow motorway to cut through the Polish capital.

The ministry said it was against plans by the government's Motorway Construction Agency (ABiEA), which wanted the road to go through residential areas either on the south or north of Warsaw, saying other solutions were not financially feasible.
"A decision supporting a bypass inside (Warsaw)...would essentially give a priority to economic criteria over environmental criteria," the ministry said in a statement.

The environment ministry spokeswoman Katrzyna Karpinska said the minister would like the motorway to go through the town of Gora Kalwaria, some 30 km south of Warsaw, a route opposed by the motorway agency.
The agency says it would be difficult to secure financing for a motorway routed outside Warsaw because investors would not be able to benefit from heavy traffic, forecast to be directed to Warsaw.

Under the government programme, investors selected in public tenders are entitled to collect tolls on motorways they construct for up to 25 years. The government is to provide some 15 percent of the financing.

The final decision on the motorway's route, part of an $8 billion scheme to build 2,500 km of toll motorways in 15 years, rests with the interior minister, who will analyse opinions of other ministers, ABiEA and local governments.
The interior ministry officials were not available for comment on when the long-awaited decision would be taken.
